question: The courier prints a line, then records the delivery. Stopped between the two, is the message lost?
The courier marks a message acknowledged when it carries it, so the latency reading is the round trip?
premise_flaw: The courier never writes an acknowledgment. Printing the line is delivery and nothing more; only the recipient's own `ack` records that a session read it, so queued-to-delivered and delivered-to-acked are two readings and not one round trip.
